instruction: Find youth Nike sweatpants between $40 and $80.

metadata.explanation: Variation of NBA store filtering task. User must apply 4 filters: youth category, Nike brand, sweatpants type, and $40-$80 price range. Evaluator checks all filters are present in HTML class elements and URL parameters, with no extra filters.
metadata.verification: Reuses existing check_direct_json_object metric and get_active_tab_html_parse getter. Pattern matches original task structure.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete coverage: Evaluator checks all 4 filter requirements from the instruction (youth, Nike, sweatpants, $40-$80 price range)
Logical correctness: Getter extracts filter state from both HTML class elements and URL parameters using case-insensitive matching
Correct verification logic: The 'class&url' category checks for expected filters in both DOM elements and URL, ensuring filters are actually applied
No extra filters check: Validates 'is_other_exist: false' to ensure no unexpected filters are present
Metric correctly compares all expected keys with actual values using check_direct_json_object
Data flow is sound: getter extracts filter JSON -> metric compares with expected -> returns 1.0 only if all filters match
Practical feasibility: Active tab HTML/URL is accessible via Playwright, e-commerce sites typically expose filter state in both DOM and URL
No postconfig needed: Filter state persists in page after user interaction
